text:
Anya: FYI I enabled FP8 kernels on a small L40S test pool overnight. Running the standard quant bakeoff suite (WebText longprefix + codebench). Seeing a reproducible tiny quality delta on long-prefix tests.

Mike: can you paste the numbers? short-context vs long?

Anya: short (512): delta ~+0.4% ppl, long (2048/4096): +2.0% ppl and occasional decoder garble (broken tokens at prefix boundaries).

Lee: I grabbed a few traces. Looks like intermittent accumulator overflow prior to layernorm for some matmul tiles on L40S. H100 runs the same model with fp8 and is clean.

Mike: trace excerpt:
```
ERROR: fp8_accumulator: scale overflow at matmul tile (dim 128x64)
module: transformer.layers.35.attn
dtype: fp8_e4m3
note: subsequent layernorm received infs -> fallback triggered
```

Sara: interesting. Could be tiling + accumulation width differences on L40S. We saw something similar with int8 path ages ago.

Anya: what are options? full disable FP8 on L40S, per-layer fallback, or kernel tweak?

Lee: three paths:
1) runtime shim that monitors per-layer stat windows and switches that layer to fp16 if it sees scale blowouts.
2) kernel patch: increase accumulator headroom and add pre-layernorm clamp for L40S matmul path.
3) conservative quant profile (narrow dynamic range) for L40S which may lose perf.

Mike: perf delta matters. On H100 fp8 gave us ~2x throughput, but L40S kernel tweak should preserve most gains if we avoid global fallback.

Sara: I prototyped a shim config you can toggle in canary:
```
quant_runtime:
  fp8_enabled: true
  per_layer_watch: true
  window: 64
  overflow_threshold: 0.5
  fallback_dtype: fp16
  fallback_actions: [layer, kernel]
```
Canary toggle is "quant_runtime.canary_mode".

Anya: canary plan suggestion:
- Stage 1: enable shim on all hosts but only active on L40S test pool (1% traffic) for 24h
- Stage 2: deploy kernel patch to 1 L40S host running synthetic longprefix workload (2048/4096)
- Stage 3: if kernel looks ok, expand to L40S pool at 5% before retiring shim
Observability: need per-layer overflow rate, fallback fraction, ppl diffs per eval bucket.

Mike: I ran quick runs vs baseline. With shim on L40S: throughput -5%, p95 +8ms, long perplexity delta down to +0.6% (so shim helps). Kernel patch local sim reduces delta to +0.2% and perf ~-1% vs ideal fp8.

Lee: I'll open a kernel PR to widen accumulator lanes and insert a clamp before layernorm for fp8 path on L40S. Will include microbench and a longseq regression test.

Sara: I'll wire alerting: alert if fallback_fraction > 0.3% for >10m, and record a "degraded decode" metric if we see invalid token sequences.

Anya: ticket please so we can track. Also include GPTQ/AWQ variants in the bakeoff matrix for longprefix; we need to know whether model-side quant guts interact with runtime fp8.

Mike: filed INFR-3410 with traces, eval diffs, and bench numbers. Added experiment matrix: [FP8, INT8-GPTQ, INT8-AWQ] x [H100, L40S] x [512, 2048, 4096].

infra-bot: deploy-bot: started canary quant_runtime.canary_mode=true on pool=l40s-test at 2025-12-03T07:12Z

Lee: test note: the overflow is sensitive to weight outliers in a few heads. Adding a per-head clamp helped in sim; we'll test head-clamp vs full-matmul-clamp.

Sara: ops note: if we fallback many layers we'll hit fp16 memory increase; set a cap of 3 layers fallback per request to avoid OOMs.

Mike: running the full matrix overnight. Early peek: AWQ-int8 tends to keep long-perplexity closer than GPTQ for this checkpoint, but AWQ incurrs extra prepack time.

Anya: thanks. Let's regroup in standup. Priority is avoid user-facing regressions while keeping fp8 perf where safe. If kernel patch verifies we can remove the shim in week+.

deploy-bot: canary update: l40s-test fallback_rate=0.12% after 3h, healthy. h100 baseline unchanged.

Lee: PR queued: rwd/runtime#5420 (kernel accum widen + clamp) - CI includes longseq regression that reproduces the original failure locally.

Sara: I'll add observability dashboard panels: layer_overflow_rate, fallback_fraction, degraded_decode_rate, ppl_longprefix_delta.

Anya: excellent. Appreciate the quick triage. We'll aim to ship kernel fix behind a runtime flag and rollback path. :thumbsup:
